revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Four elements of the contactor driver: the close request, the state read, the feedback check and the unconditional open sweep. Two findings are recorded from the source rather than smoothed over: STD_NOT_OK is ambiguous between a refused request and a registry miss, and the feedback check carries an open TODO about contactor-type uniqueness per string.

providing_module.name: Contactor driver
providing_module.role: Acts on the contactors and reads their feedback. It keeps the commanded state and the feedback separately and forwards actuation requests to the SPS module.

consuming_modules.name: BMS state machine
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: The state machine is the only consumer. CONT_OpenAllPrechargeContactors at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L1045, CONT_OpenContactor at L1070 and L1086, CONT_GetContactorState at L1094 and L1303, CONT_CloseContactor at L1281 and L1328, CONT_OpenAllContactors at L1160 and CONT_CheckFeedback at L917.

consuming_modules.name: SPS module, the downstream actuator interface
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: The close request forwards to SPS_RequestContactorState(cont_contactorStates[contactorIndex].spsChannel, SPS_CHANNEL_ON) at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L195 and the implementation discards that call's return value.

elements.declaration: extern STD_RETURN_TYPE_e CONT_CloseContactor(uint8_t stringNumber, CONT_TYPE_e contactor);

parameters.name: stringNumber
parameters.meaning: The string the contactor belongs to.
parameters.range_evidence: FAS_ASSERT(stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L185. BS_NR_OF_STRINGS is (1u) at src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h L109.

parameters.name: contactor
parameters.meaning: Which kind of contactor of that string to act on: the plus contactor, the minus contactor or the precharge contactor.

values.STD_OK: A matching contactor was found in the registry and the requested state was set on it.
values.STD_NOT_OK: No contactor in the registry matched the string and type pair, so nothing was set.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: No third value exists. STD_NOT_OK is returned both when the request was refused and when the registry simply has no such contactor, so a caller cannot tell a configuration mistake from a busy resource.
return_contract.evidence: src/app/main/include/fstd_types.h L82-L85; the two return paths are at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L196 and L187/L200.

validity_signalling.evidence: STD_OK is set only inside the loop after a registry match, at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L196; the initial value STD_NOT_OK at L187 is returned unchanged if the loop completes without a match, at L200.

timing.evidence: Called from the BMS state machine, which runs on the 10 ms cyclic task: for example CONT_CloseContactor(bms_state.firstClosedString, CONT_MINUS) at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L1281. FTSK_TASK_CYCLIC_10MS_CYCLE_TIME is 10u at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L112.

concurrency.evidence: Reached from the BMS state machine in src/app/application/bms/bms.c; no interrupt context reaches this entry point in the source.

error_paths.condition: stringNumber is at or above BS_NR_OF_STRINGS.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: A precondition assertion trips before the loop.
A precondition assertion trips before the loop.

error_paths.condition: No registry entry matches the string and type pair.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The loop completes without a match, the initial STD_NOT_OK is returned, and no contactor state is changed.

not_specified_by_source: The interface returns STD_OK when the request has been placed on a registry entry, not when the contactor has closed. Nothing here reports the resulting electrical state; that is what CONT_GetContactorState and CONT_CheckFeedback are for, and neither is named by this element.

The interface does not state that the request is forwarded to the SPS module by name or what happens if that forward fails. The forward is SPS_RequestContactorState(..., SPS_CHANNEL_ON) at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L195 and its return value is not read, so a failure inside the SPS module is invisible here.

The interface does not state BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS, the size of the registry it searches. That is (2u * BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) + BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS_OUTSIDE_STRINGS at src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h L237.

The interface does not state whether a request for a contactor that is already closed is idempotent, accepted or rejected. The implementation sets the same field and returns STD_OK, so it is idempotent in effect, but that is not stated.

elements.declaration: extern CONT_ELECTRICAL_STATE_TYPE_e CONT_GetContactorState(uint8_t stringNumber, CONT_TYPE_e contactorType);

parameters.name: stringNumber
parameters.meaning: The string the contactor belongs to.

parameters.name: contactorType
parameters.meaning: Which kind of contactor of that string to read.

values.CONT_SWITCH_UNDEFINED: Initialised as the value to return and returned unchanged when no registry entry matches the string and type pair.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: CONT_SWITCH_UNDEFINED is the documented default: the local variable feedback is initialised to it at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L249 and returned at L258 if the loop finds no match. A caller therefore gets an explicit 'no such contactor' rather than a stale state.
return_contract.evidence: The declaration and its doxygen @return of 'current state, taken from #CONT_ELECTRICAL_STATE_TYPE_e' at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.h L69-L77.

validity_signalling.evidence: The no-match case returns CONT_SWITCH_UNDEFINED, so a caller can detect it: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L249 and L258.

timing.evidence: Called from the BMS state machine in src/app/application/bms/bms.c, for example at L1094 and L1303; that state machine runs on the 10 ms cyclic task.

concurrency.evidence: Reached from the BMS state machine in src/app/application/bms/bms.c; no interrupt context reaches it in the source.

error_paths.condition: No registry entry matches the pair.
stringNumber is out of range or contactorType is CONT_UNDEFINED.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: A precondition assertion trips before the loop.

not_specified_by_source: The interface returns the contactor's feedback field, not its commanded set field. The source keeps the two separately, as currentSet and feedback, and this element exposes only the feedback, so a caller can read what the contactor reports but not what it was told to do. Nothing in this element states the distinction.

The interface does not state the size of the registry it searches or what the caller's obligations are if more than one contactor of the same type is registered for a string. The driver carries a TODO saying it does not check that only one contactor of each type is configured for each string.
The interface states no timing expectation: it does not say how stale the feedback may be, so a caller cannot distinguish a contactor that is slow from one that has failed.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: Not applicable as a return value, and that is itself the contract weakness: the function reports nothing to its caller. Its only output is the side effect of registering diagnosis events with the DIAG module.
return_contract.evidence: Declared void in the source; the interface communicates entirely through side effects.

validity_signalling.mechanism: Side effect: one diagnosis event per configured contactor, with the event value derived by comparing the commanded state with the feedback.
validity_signalling.evidence: Declared void at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.h L128. The body computes feedbackStatus by comparing currentSet with feedback at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L132 and then registers a diagnosis event per contactor, for DIAG_ID_STRING_PLUS_CONTACTOR_FEEDBACK at L138, DIAG_ID_STRING_MINUS_CONTACTOR_FEEDBACK at L145 and DIAG_ID_PRECHARGE_CONTACTOR_FEEDBACK at L152.

timing.evidence: Called at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L917 from BMS_Trigger, in the 10 ms cyclic task, FTSK_TASK_CYCLIC_10MS_CYCLE_TIME 10u at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L112.

concurrency.evidence: Reached only from BMS_Trigger at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L917, in the 10 ms cyclic task.

error_paths.condition: A contactor's feedback does not match what it was commanded to do.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: A DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK is registered for the diagnosis id matching that contactor type; a match registers DIAG_EVENT_OK.
error_paths.signalled_as: diagnosis event, not a return value
error_paths.evidence: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L131-L135 and the three DIAG_Handler calls at L138, L145 and L152

error_paths.condition: A registry entry has a type outside CONT_PLUS, CONT_MINUS and CONT_PRECHARGE.
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The switch falls to its default branch and a precondition assertion traps.

not_specified_by_source: The interface reports a mismatch as a diagnosis event and nothing else, so a caller cannot distinguish 'contactor open when it should be closed' from 'contactor closed when it should be open'. The diagnosis id and the string index are passed, and the polarity is lost at this boundary.

The interface does not state how many contactors it checks. The body iterates BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS, defined as (2u * BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) + BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS_OUTSIDE_STRINGS at src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h L237.

The source carries an open item in the interface itself: a TODO in the body at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L130 saying that a check that only one contactor of each type is configured for each string is still to be added. The interface therefore does not guarantee that a string has exactly one contactor per type, and this record does not claim it does.
The interface does not state a debounce or a settling time, so it does not say whether a transient mismatch during switching is expected to be reported.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: Not applicable as a return value, and that is itself the contract weakness: the function reports nothing to its caller. Its only output is the side effect of registering diagnosis events with the DIAG module.
return_contract.evidence: Declared void in the source; the interface communicates entirely through side effects.

validity_signalling.mechanism: None returned. The effect is a sweep over the contactor registry.
validity_signalling.evidence: Declared void at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.h L121; the implementation iterates the registry and opens each entry.

timing.evidence: Called at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L1160 from BMS_Trigger, in the 10 ms cyclic task.

concurrency.evidence: Reached only from BMS_Trigger at src/app/application/bms/bms.c L1160, in the 10 ms cyclic task.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: No error path is observable; the function has no return value and registers no diagnosis event of its own.
error_paths.evidence: The body at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L236-L244 opens every registry entry and returns.

not_specified_by_source: The interface is unconditional and unchecked. It opens every registered contactor including any that sit outside a string, because the registry size includes BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS_OUTSIDE_STRINGS, and it says nothing about that.
The interface reports nothing, so a caller cannot know whether the sweep completed or which contactors were affected.
The interface states no relationship to the precharge contactors: CONT_OpenAllPrechargeContactors is a separate function in the same header, and the two are not distinguished here.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The interface never reports the electrical outcome of a request. Closing returns STD_OK when the request is placed on a registry entry, and the electrical state is a separate read through CONT_GetContactorState.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: No single element of this interface lets a caller close a contactor and learn that it closed. A requirement about actuation has to be written across two elements, and the source does not state the pair as a contract.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: STD_OK is set at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L196 immediately after the SPS forward at L195, with no confirmation of the resulting state.

interface_level_gaps.gap: STD_NOT_OK is ambiguous between two different situations.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: A caller cannot distinguish a configuration error, which no amount of retrying will fix, from a transient condition. A requirement that says the interface shall report failure distinctly per cause is not satisfiable against this implementation.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The initial STD_NOT_OK at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L187 is returned unchanged both when the loop finds no matching registry entry, at L200, and on the path where the forward to the SPS module has already been made.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The forward to the actuator is unchecked.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: A failure reported by the SPS module does not reach the caller of the contactor interface, so the interface cannot signal it.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: SPS_RequestContactorState is called at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L195 and its return value is not assigned or tested on the following lines.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The feedback interface carries an open item in the source itself.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: The interface does not guarantee one contactor per type per string, so a caller reading a contactor state may be reading an arbitrary one of several.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The TODO at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L130 states that the check that only one contactor of each type is configured for each string is still to be added.
